LESSON: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we read using technology?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read grade- appropriate digital poems and narratives of about 300- 320 words interpretively for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read grade- appropriate digital poems and narratives of about 300- 320 words interpretively for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to read grade- appropriate digital poems and narratives of about 300- 320 words interpretively for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read grade- appropriate digital poems and narratives of about 300- 320 words interpretively for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read grade- appropriate digital poems and narratives of about 300- 320 words interpretively for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read grade- appropriate digital poems and narratives of about 300- 320 words interpretively for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read grade- appropriate digital poems and narratives of about 300- 320 words interpretively for comprehension.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read using technology?
2. How do you search for information using technology?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read grade- appropriate digital poems and narratives of about 300- 320 words interpretively for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
